definitions.explanation: An egg cell that has been fertilized by a sperm cell — used in biology, reproductive medicine, and everyday discussion of pregnancy, IVF, and animal breeding. Also used for fertilized eggs of birds (e.g., chickens) that will develop into chicks if incubated.

examples.japanese: {受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{子宮|しきゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{着床|ちゃくしょう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The fertilized egg implanted in the uterus.

examples.japanese: ⟦{体外|たいがい}{受精|じゅせい}→体外受精：26496_taigaijusei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{作|つく}られた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧{受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{凍結保存|とうけつほぞん}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The fertilized eggs created through IVF were cryopreserved.

examples.japanese: ニワトリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{温|あたた}める→温める：02096_atatameru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧21⟦{日|にち}→日：12732_nichi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ヒヨコ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれる→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧。
examples.english: If you incubate a chicken's fertilized egg, a chick hatches in about 21 days.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{受精|じゅせい}→受精：29502_jusei⟧ (fertilization) and {卵|らん} (egg, in its Sino-Japanese reading). The kanji {卵|らん} is read らん only in compounds; the standalone noun for "egg" is ⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧: a fertilized egg forms
- {受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{着床|ちゃくしょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: the fertilized egg implants
- {受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{培養|ばいよう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to culture a fertilized egg
- {受精卵|じゅせいらん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{凍結|とうけつ}→凍結：09613_touketsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to freeze a fertilized egg
- ⟦{体外|たいがい}{受精|じゅせい}→体外受精：26496_taigaijusei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{受精卵|じゅせいらん}: IVF-created fertilized egg

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{受精|じゅせい}→受精：29502_jusei⟧: fertilization
- {卵子|らんし}: ovum, egg cell (before fertilization)
- {精子|せいし}: sperm
- {胚|はい}: embryo — what the {受精卵|じゅせいらん} develops into
- {無精卵|むせいらん}: unfertilized egg — the antonym, commonly used for supermarket chicken eggs
